intro: Here at Patara, an ancient city in Antalya province, the story reaches back to the 5th century BC. This was the capital of the Lycian League, and home to what may be the world's first parliament building.
history: Patara was Lycia's principal port and the seat of an oracle of Apollo. It became the Roman provincial capital, and then, for centuries, it lay preserved beneath sand dunes.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Bouleuterion, the assembly building, and the Triumphal Arch; then visit the theatre, the lighthouse and the colonnaded street.
facts: Did you know? Saint Nicholas, better known as Santa Claus, was born here around AD 270. The Lycian League met in the council house here, and its system, with delegates voting in proportion to their city's size, reached the American constitutional debates as a model of federalism, by way of Montesquieu. And the lighthouse, raised under Nero, is among the oldest surviving anywhere; its blocks were found and reassembled.
outro: This brings our tour of Patara to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
